title: Avoiding unsafe type assertions
description: Learn why type assertions can be dangerous and how to replace them with safer patterns in React and TypeScript.

data.text: A type assertion tells TypeScript to treat a value as a specific type, even when the compiler cannot verify it. It is like a promise you make to the compiler: 'Trust me, I know this is a string.' If your promise is wrong, the compiler will not catch it and the bug will appear at runtime.
The Cost of Lying to the Compiler

Type assertions remove safety. When you assert a value is a type without proving it, you bypass the narrowing logic that would otherwise catch mistakes. This is especially risky in React components where props or state might come from external sources.

data.title: Unsafe Assertion Example
data.content: Asserting without validation can crash your app

data.text: Instead of asserting, validate. A type guard or schema validation proves the shape of the data before you use it. The compiler stays honest, and invalid data produces a clear error instead of a silent crash.

data.title: Replace Assertion with Validation
data.content: Using a type guard instead of as

data.text: Assertions are not evil. They are useful in three situations: when you have already validated the data earlier, when you interact with a library that TypeScript cannot understand, or when the assertion is trivial and obviously correct.

items: After a successful schema parse, the data is already validated
When DOM APIs return `any` and you know the element exists
For simple literals that the compiler cannot infer

data.title: Acceptable Assertion After Validation
Avoid as Unknown as Any
data.text: The pattern `value as unknown as SomeType` bypasses all type checking. It is a code smell that usually means the types are wrong somewhere. Fix the types instead of forcing the compiler to ignore the mismatch.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Type assertions bypass compiler checks and can hide bugs
Prefer type guards or schema validation over assertions
Assertions are acceptable only after prior validation
Avoid `as unknown as SomeType` as a workaround
data.takeaway: Replace assertions with validations and let TypeScript prove correctness instead of assuming it.
